svg.title: Bohemia Spillway: four different kinds of public records, 1924 to 2025
svg.desc: An original Final Vestige documentary chronology. In 1924 to 1926, the Orleans Levee Board acquired roughly 33,000 acres by multiple methods. A 1984 Louisiana law ordered return of eligible former private land. In July 2024 a later authority delegated administration of mineral leasing on remaining district lands. In February 2025 managers said Bohemia generated 47,000 dollars in revenue during 2024. The records concern different interests and do not establish that every former private parcel is still held or that any specific heir remains unpaid. Sources are Louisiana Supreme Court 1986 and Lakefront Management Authority approved July 25 2024 and February 20 2025 minutes, catalogued in the accompanying investigation.
svg.text: The Land Changed Hands. The Records Kept Going.
Bohemia Spillway, 1924–2025 · four distinct documentary claims

g.text: Approx. 33,000 acres entered through distinct acquisition routes.

Act 233 directed return of qualifying acquired private lands.

The authority approved delegation of mineral-leasing administration.
Applies to district-owned interests, not automatically every old parcel.
Board staff reported $47,000 in Bohemia revenue for 2024.
Management figure; not an audited parcel or claimant payment ledger.
